name: go-app-ui-semantic-accessibility-audit-and-6db5
instr:
go-app cannot audit UI-tree accessibility semantics before browser mounting without losing representation context in encoded HTML. Add first-class auditing to github.com/maxence-charriere/go-app/v11/pkg/app through `AuditUI`, `NewAuditPolicy`, and `Raw`, sharing policy and report semantics across direct inspection, `NewTestEngine`, HTTP rendering, and `GenerateStaticWebsiteWithAudit`.

Audit every built-in UI representation deterministically without mutation. Order findings by Path, then by Rule. Report unsupported custom representations and missing component roots instead of omitting them or panicking. Render components once without browser lifecycle callbacks. Preserve selected-condition branch identity and stable range indices or sorted map keys. Cover HTML tags, attributes, handlers, namespaces, self-closing state, and ordered children. Built-in rules cover landmarks, heading progression, form labels, interactive names, image alternatives, and duplicate identifiers.

`AuditPolicy` filters rules and sets `AuditReport.Blocked` without changing finding identity or order. `NewAuditPolicy()` returns the default policy, and `AuditUI(ui, policy)` returns the report. When configured, Handler audits each pre-rendered page and rejects its response with a server error if and only if the report is blocked. `AuditObserver(page, report)` receives exactly one complete report per audited HTTP page, including blocked pages.
